handbookNote: Oklahoma Real Estate Broker license exam. Part of the 2026-09-02 R26 population-tier broker buildout. Exam vendor: PSI, under contract with the Oklahoma Real Estate Commission (OREC). PRIMARY-CONFIRMED by directly downloading and reading PSI's own official Oklahoma Real Estate Licensure Applicant Information Bulletin (Copyright 2018, last revised 12/1/2018 -- current bulletin as of this build). Exam mechanics: Broker exam = 135 items, scored up to 140 points (a small number of scenario-based items are worth up to 2 points each -- see the bulletin's own scored sample scenario), 4 hours, 75% (105/140 points) to pass. track_registry models this as exam_question_count=135, exam_duration_sec=14400, pass_percent=75, min_correct=105 (140 x 0.75 = 105 exactly; this is a points threshold, not a straight question count, given the 2-point scenario items -- flagged here since it's a genuine mechanical nuance of this exam, not a simplification). Broker eligibility: 2 years active experience as a Provisional Sales Associate or Sales Associate within the preceding 5 years (or an Equivalent Point Application waiver), plus 90 clock hours of advanced broker-course instruction. NATIONAL PORTION (75 items, PSI's real Oklahoma-specific weighting of its standard 11-section outline -- these percentages differ from Kentucky's raw item counts for the same 11 sections, confirming PSI customizes weights per state even though the section names are shared): I. Property Ownership (10%), II. Land Use Controls and Regulations (5%), III. Valuation and Market Analysis (7%), IV. Financing (8%), V. General Principles of Agency (11%), VI. Property Disclosures (7%), VII. Contracts (18%, the largest section), VIII. Leasing and Property Management (5%), IX. Transfer of Title (7%), X. Practice of Real Estate (14%), XI. Real Estate Calculations (8%). Oklahoma's outline has no separate 'Specialty Areas' section (unlike Kentucky's). Section IX (Transfer of Title) was missed in the initial 8-topic drafting pass and added as a same-day gap-fill once the real official outline was fetched and read in full. OKLAHOMA STATE PORTION (60 items, per the same bulletin): Laws and Rules Affecting Oklahoma Real Estate Practice (20), Oklahoma Broker Relationships Act (10 -- Oklahoma's distinctive statutory scheme: OREC's own bulletin explicitly notes brokers here do NOT practice under the 'common law of agency' at all with consumers, only broker-relationship duties defined by statute, one of the most exam-relevant, counterintuitive facts in this track and directly tested by the drafting agent), Property Management (7), Disclosures and Hazards (5), Trust Accounts and Trust Funds (8), Broker Management (10). Sourced against the Oklahoma Real Estate Commission's own official 'Code and Rules Book' (Nov 1, 2025 edition -- OREC's consolidated publication of 59 O.S. Chapter 20 (Real Estate License Code) plus OAC Title 605 administrative rules), downloaded as a PDF and read directly with pdftotext since WebFetch's PDF-to-markdown conversion garbled it -- every state-portion citation in this bank traces to that single primary document. One scrivener's-error correction was caught: OREC's own official disclosure form cites the Residential Property Condition Disclosure Act's 'Defect' definition as '59 O.S. Section 832(9)' even though the Act itself is codified in Title 60 (confirmed via OSCN, the official Oklahoma statute host) -- the drafting agent used '60 O.S.' rather than propagate OREC's own apparent typo. This bank was drafted across 13 parallel single-topic drafting passes (8 national + 5 state-law categories) plus a same-day 9th national gap-fill, each instructed to draft as many genuinely distinct, real, grounded questions as its topic's source material supports with NO target number or ceiling. Answers were deterministically rotated into final A/B/C/D position via scripts/tracks/rotate_broker_answers.js, producing a final near-even 25.0/25.0/25.0/24.9% A/B/C/D distribution. 659 raw questions drafted against a 135-item exam -- a 4.88:1 pool ratio, just under the standing 5:1 target but well clear of the 4:1 floor.
